title: Place Value to a Billion and Decimals to Hundredths
seo_title: Grade 4 Place Value to a Billion Worksheets: Expanded Notation (TEKS 4.2A, 4.2B, STAAR)
standard_text: 4.2A interpret the value of each place-value position as 10 times the position to the right and as one-tenth of the value of the place to its left; 4.2B represent the value of the digit in whole numbers through 1,000,000,000 and decimals to the hundredths using expanded notation and numerals
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 place value worksheets for Texas TEKS 4.2A and 4.2B: read and write numbers to a billion, value of a digit, 10 times and one tenth relationships with decimals, and expanded notation. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Each place is 10 times the place to its right.
key_sub: Read big numbers by periods: billions, millions, thousands, ones. Each place is also one tenth of the place to its left.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Large numbers are read in groups of 3 digits (periods): billions, millions, thousands, ones. 2,045,300,016 is two billion, forty-five million, three hundred thousand, sixteen.
  • Each place is 10 times the place to its right and one tenth of the place to its left. This works for decimals too: 0.3 is 10 times 0.03.
  • Expanded notation writes each digit times its place value: (4 × 1,000,000) + (7 × 1,000) + (2 × 1).

Examples

Example

Write 30,506,000 in words.

30 million

506 thousand

Answer: thirty million, five hundred six thousand

Example

What is one tenth of 0.6?

Move each digit one place right.

Answer: 0.06

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Dropping a zero: 30,506,000 as 3,506,000Each period after the first has exactly 3 digits.
Reading the digit, not its valueThe 7 in 7,000,000 is worth 7 million.
Thinking each place is 10 times the place to its leftMoving left multiplies by 10; moving right divides by 10.

faq.a: Interpret the value of each place as 10 times the position to the right and one tenth of the position to the left, including numbers through billions and decimals to hundredths.
Represent the value of a digit in whole numbers through 1,000,000,000 and decimals to hundredths with expanded notation and numerals.
A group of 3 places: ones, thousands, millions, billions. Commas separate the periods.

faq.q: How do place values work for decimals?
faq.a: Tenths are one tenth of ones, and hundredths are one tenth of tenths.

sets.title: Each place is 10 times the place to its right

items.q: What is 10 × 6,000?
items.e: Multiplying by 10 moves each digit one place to the left: 6 thousands become 6 ten thousands. 6,000 × 10 = 60,000.

items.q: What is 10 × 400?
items.e: Multiplying by 10 moves each digit one place to the left: 4 hundreds become 4 thousands. 400 × 10 = 4,000.
Multiplying by 10 moves each digit one place to the left: 9 ten thousands become 9 hundred thousands. 90,000 × 10 = 900,000.
Multiplying by 10 moves each digit one place to the left: 1 hundred thousand becomes 1 million. 100,000 × 10 = 1,000,000.
Dividing by 10 moves each digit one place to the right: 7 ten thousands become 7 thousands. 70,000 ÷ 10 = 7,000.

items.q: What is 5,000 ÷ 10?
items.e: Dividing by 10 moves each digit one place to the right: 5 thousands become 5 hundreds. 5,000 ÷ 10 = 500.
Dividing by 10 moves each digit one place to the right: 2 hundred thousands become 2 ten thousands. 200,000 ÷ 10 = 20,000.

items.q: 800 is 10 times as much as what number?
items.e: Ask: 10 times what number is 800? One place to the right of the hundreds place is the tens place, so the answer is 80. Check: 10 × 80 = 800.

items.q: 30,000 is 10 times as much as what number?

items.q: Look at the two 3s in 133,799. The 3 on the left is worth how many times as much as the 3 on the right?
